mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs compressing equity discounting.
failure_condition: In high-interest-rate regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) after controlling for inflation and risk factors.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% in a month followed by a stabilization signals disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as market expectations for future inflation normalize.
failure_condition: Over 100 observations, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) after adjusting for lagged inflation expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and a decline in unemployment (implied via UNRATE falling by ≥0.2 percentage points) over two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: In tightening labor markets, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) after accounting for sector-specific volatility.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% for three consecutive months is accompanied by a rise in retail sales (implied via HOUST), predicting a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO[t] > INDPRO[t-1] * 1.02 and INDPRO[t+1] >= INDPRO[t] * 1.02 and INDPRO[t+2] >= INDPRO[t+1] * 1.02 and HOUST[t] > HOUST[t-1]
failure_condition: During expansionary regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) after controlling for sector-specific news.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month, followed by two consecutive months of contraction, predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it reflects weakening supply-side conditions and reduced earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO[t] < INDPRO[t-1] * 0.97 and INDPRO[t+1] < INDPRO[t] * 0.97 and INDPRO[t+2] < INDPRO[t+1] * 0.97
failure_condition: In supply-constrained regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after adjusting for commodity price shocks.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 0.1 percentage points for two consecutive months during a period of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL[t] > CPIAUCSL[t-1] + 0.5 and UNRATE[t] > UNRATE[t-1] + 0.1 and UNRATE[t+1] > UNRATE[t] + 0.1
failure_condition: In inflationary regimes, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after controlling for inflation surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in labor force participation (implied via PAYEMS falling by ≥2% for two months) in a recessionary regime is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals demographic headwinds and weak wage growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS[t] < PAYEMS[t-1] * 0.98 and PAYEMS[t+1] < PAYEMS[t] * 0.98 and regime: 'recessionary'
failure_condition: During recessions, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after adjusting for sector-specific risk premia.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in retail activity (HOUST) and manufacturing activity (RSAFS) by at least 5% in the same month predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as it reflects broad-based demand recovery.
failure_condition: In dual-sector acceleration periods, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) after controlling for sector-specific news and macroeconomic regime effects.
